testSet.name: sprint planning
testSet.prompt: Ana: okay so the checkout rewrite is behind, we said two weeks and it's been four. Ben: the payment provider sandbox was down for three days, that's most of it. Ana: fine but we need a date. Ben: end of next week if nothing else breaks. Ana: I'll tell the client Friday the 14th then. Also Priya, can you take over the analytics dashboard from Ben so he can focus? Priya: yes, I'll pick it up Monday.
testSet.expected: Checkout rewrite is two weeks late, mostly due to a three-day payment sandbox outage. New target: end of next week; client will be told Friday the 14th. Priya takes over the analytics dashboard from Ben starting Monday so Ben can focus on checkout.

testSet.name: incident review
testSet.prompt: Sam: the outage lasted 47 minutes, started when the migration locked the orders table. Dev: we ran it during peak instead of the maintenance window. Sam: why? Dev: the runbook says maintenance window but nobody checked it. Sam: so the fix is enforcement, not the runbook. Dev: right, I'll add a CI check that blocks migrations outside the window. Sam: due by end of sprint.
testSet.expected: A 47-minute outage was caused by a migration locking the orders table during peak traffic, run outside the documented maintenance window because nobody checked the runbook. The fix is enforcement rather than documentation: a CI check blocking out-of-window migrations, due by end of sprint.

testSet.name: hiring debrief
testSet.prompt: Rae: candidate was strong on system design, weaker on the SQL round. Tom: how weak? Rae: couldn't write a window function without help, but reasoned well once nudged. Tom: for a senior backend role that's borderline. Rae: agreed, but the design round was the best I've seen this quarter. Tom: let's do one more technical screen focused on data, then decide. Rae: I'll schedule it this week.
testSet.expected: The candidate was strong in system design — the best of the quarter — but weak on SQL, needing help with window functions though reasoning well when nudged. That is borderline for a senior backend role, so the decision is deferred pending one more data-focused technical screen, which Rae will schedule this week.

testSet.name: roadmap sync
testSet.prompt: Kim: we can't do both the mobile app and the API v2 this quarter. Jo: sales wants mobile, the biggest three customers want API v2. Kim: revenue attached? Jo: API v2 accounts for about 400k of renewals, mobile is prospective. Kim: then API v2 first, mobile slips to Q3. Jo: I'll rewrite the roadmap and tell sales today.
testSet.expected: Mobile and API v2 cannot both ship this quarter. API v2 wins because it is tied to roughly $400k of renewals from the three biggest customers, while mobile revenue is only prospective. Mobile slips to Q3; Jo updates the roadmap and informs sales today.

testSet.name: budget call (unseen)
testSet.prompt: Nina: infra spend is up 60% quarter over quarter. Raj: most of it is the staging cluster, it runs 24/7 and nobody uses it at night. Nina: can we schedule it down? Raj: yes, off between 8pm and 7am, saves maybe 30%. Nina: do it this week. Also cancel the second monitoring vendor, we're paying twice for the same dashboards. Raj: I'll cancel at renewal on the 30th.
testSet.expected: Infrastructure spend rose 60% quarter over quarter, driven mainly by a staging cluster running 24/7 while unused overnight. Raj will schedule it off between 8pm and 7am this week for roughly 30% savings, and will cancel the duplicate second monitoring vendor at its renewal on the 30th.

testSet.name: support retro (unseen)
testSet.prompt: Ivo: ticket volume doubled after the release. Mel: 70% are about the new login flow. Ivo: same complaint? Mel: yes — the magic link expires in 5 minutes and people miss it. Ivo: that's a product bug, not a support problem. Mel: engineering says raising it to 30 minutes is a one-line change. Ivo: get it in the next patch and I'll write a canned response until then.
testSet.expected: Ticket volume doubled after the release, with 70% about the new login flow: magic links expire after 5 minutes and users miss them. It is a product bug rather than a support issue, and engineering says extending to 30 minutes is a one-line change to land in the next patch. Ivo will write a canned response in the meantime.
